title: Work songs: tasks, boss and singing to the hammer
summary: Maxey lists work done while singing, defines boss as foreman, and explains how songs fit the task and ease the day.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about the work songs, too. What different kind of works can you be doing while you sing?

Well, I mean, it can be cutting cane, or you can be ditching, maybe cutting wood, or maybe sawing. It could be using the hammers. There's plenty of different work you could be doing while you're singing.
Well, what do you call the captain and the warden and the guards and all the different kind of work?

Well, the most of the things that gives the warden name, that generally calls him just as what he is. Also, the captain, that gives them the name of what they are. So some of them call them different names, usually like a man would do. But they ain't gonna hardly call them out of their name.
Well, who do you call boss, you know? I hear that expression you used on one of the songs.
Well, that's the man that's your foreman. In other words, that's your employer. That's the man who you workin' under you. That's the man that's over you.

And this I Got Five Long Years by James Russell and gang. Here on the record, he says, Who's that man on the big white horse? I don't know his name, but they call him boss. You know that? That would be your foreman then, huh?

I suppose you're singing Take This Hammer. That's one of the ones that you sing, I see, on the record. Uh, Alberta, I'll let you bang and grow long. What would you be singing about as you go along? You might sing about Take This Hammer. You're singing about the work you do. Now, Alberta, you're singing about women. What else might you sing?

Well, I mean, you be singing about women at the same time, but that's the same time you're singing to your hammer. You're singing to the tools that you are really working with. Singing to them. That's right. What's never that you be doing while you more than have to be singing to it? Well, it don't make no difference. You could be using the shell. You're going to catch a type of music that would follow your type of work. So, that looks like makes a man day go by easy, where he can be singing all along and working along. Makes a happy day out of a lonesome day. Sometimes you be singing, you be cutting cane. Well, you be cutting cane, you might get a little small lick, that cutting cane, and a little nice little song would just fit that lick every time that you hit with that knife, because I'm a stalker cane.
